titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§227–229: The Rules of the Guard
about: Chinggis Qahan lays down the rules of the Guard, as the chronicle tells it. §227 sets four commanders over the four turns of the day guard (Buqa, Alchidai, Dodai and Doqolqu), with rod strokes for missing a turn, exile for repeated default, and a warning to the heads of the turns not to reprimand guardsmen without counsel. §228 ranks the Guard above the officers posted outside. §229 sets the working day of the day guard and quiver-bearers, the handover to the night guard, and the night guard's standing orders, with a tale of Eljigedei seized for walking above the night guard. Grammar to watch: the converb chains in -žu/-žü, the optative in -tuγai/-tügei, the polite plural command -dqun, reflexive-possessive endings (-jan, -jen, -ban), and the decree frame keġen žarliγ bolba. Shiratori's quotation marks are only partly printed, and the notes say where one is supplied.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolžu
sentences.l: Again, Chinggis Qaγan decree becoming,
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan, issuing a decree,
sentences.n: The opening of the part: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolžu, the stock decree formula (Ming 聖旨 做着), 'decree-becoming', that is, 'issuing a decree'. bolžu is bol- 'to become' plus the converb -žu, the Ming 着. The chronicle returns to the Guard, where §§224–226 left it.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "turγaγ̇ud-un dörben kešiġüd-ün ötökülekün-i tüširün
sentences.l: "Of-day-guards four of-turns heads (acc.) appointing-when,
sentences.i: “When appointing the four heads of the turns of the day guard:
sentences.n: Shiratori's opening quotation mark stands on turγaγ̇ud-un; the speech runs to the closing mark on the fourth orotuγai (Doqolqu's line), and I carry both marks in `i`. turγaγ̇ud-un is turγaγ, 'day guard' (an inference: the Ming says 散班, 'scattered shift'), with plural -d and genitive -un. kešiġüd-ün is kešig 'turn of duty' in the plural genitive (the Ming writes 護衞, 'guards', so turn and guards are one idea). ötökülekün-i, 'the heads' (Ming 爲長的, 'those who are senior'), is read as ötögü 'old man' + the verb-maker -le- 'act as' + a participle -kün, with the accusative -i; the analysis is tentative, as for aqalažu in the last part. tüširün is tüši- 'appoint' with the converb of time -rün, 'when').

morph.gloss: day guard (inference; Ming 散班 "scattered shift") [散班每 的]
turn of duty, watch (Ming 護衞 "guards") [護衞的每(的)]

sentences.t: Buqa nigen kešig kešigten-i medežü kešigten-i žasažu orotuγai.
sentences.l: Buqa one turn, guardsmen (acc.) managing, guardsmen (acc.) putting-in-order, let-enter.
sentences.i: Let Buqa enter on duty with one turn, having charge of the guardsmen and putting them in order.
sentences.n: This unit and the next three are near-identical, one per commander (Buqa, Alchidai, Dodai, Doqolqu), each ending in the optative -tuγai ('let him …', the Ming 者). The two converbs medežü ('knowing', here 'having charge of', Ming 管着) and žasažu ('putting in order', Ming 整治着) are the converb -žü/-žu again, 'having …'; kešigten-i is the guardsmen as object (accusative -i, the Ming 行). nigen kešig, 'one turn' (Ming 一班), has neither ending nor verb of its own; I read it as the turn the commander takes and leads.

morph.gloss: guardsman, member of the guard [護衞的(每)行]
to know; here to have charge of [管着]
guardsman, member of the guard [護衞的(每)行]

sentences.t: Alčidai nigen kešig kešigten-i medežü kešigten-i žasažu orotuγai.
sentences.l: Alčidai one turn, guardsmen (acc.) managing, guardsmen (acc.) putting-in-order, let-enter.
sentences.i: Let Alchidai enter on duty with one turn, having charge of the guardsmen and putting them in order.
sentences.n: The same pattern; only the name changes. Alčidai is marked by the Ming only as 人名, 'a person's name'; the name Alchidai was already met in §§224–226.

sentences.n: Same pattern. čerbi (Ming 官名, 'an office') is left as 'cherbi', as in the last part; what the office was is not known from these glosses.

sentences.t: keġen dörben kešiġüd-ün ötöküs-i tüšižü
sentences.l: Saying, four of-turns heads (acc.) appointing,
sentences.i: Saying this, and having appointed the heads of the four turns,
sentences.n: keġen is the converb 'saying' that closes the quotation, the Ming 麽道. ötöküs-i is ötögü 'elder' with plural -s and accusative -i (the Ming 爲長的每行, 'the heads'), and tüšižü is tüši- 'appoint' + the converb -žü. This is the first link of a chain of converbs; the sentence will end at the next decree formula, and I have cut it into short units.

morph.gloss: turn of duty, watch (Ming 護衞 "guards") [班每 的]

sentences.t: kešig oroqui žarliγ tuṅγarun:
sentences.l: Turn entering decree proclaiming-when:
sentences.i: he proclaimed the decree on going on duty:
sentences.n: The quotation that begins on the next unit is the decree itself. oroqui is oro- 'enter' with the participle -qu and the vowel -i (Ming 入的, 'entering'); tuṅγarun is tuṅγa- 'proclaim' + -run 'when' (Ming 宣布). Read 'turn-entering decree' as 'the decree for entering a turn'.

sentences.t: "Kešig ororun kešig-ün nojan öġer-tür(i)-jen kešiglegsed
sentences.l: "Turn entering-when, of-turn officer, own-to-his-own, those-serving-turns,
sentences.i: “When going on duty, the officer of the turn, to his own men, those who serve the turn,
sentences.n: Shiratori opens a quotation on Kešig; I show the opening mark in `i` too. ororun is oro- + the converb of time -run, 'when entering'. nojan 'officer' (the Ming 官人) stands in the singular, kešig-ün 'of the turn' is the genitive (-ün after front vowel). öġer-tür(i)-jen is öġer 'own' + dative-locative -tür + the reflexive-possessive -jen 'his own' (Shiratori's bracketed (i) is the vowel that links them). kešiglegsed is kešig 'turn' + -le- + -gsed 'those who …', the Ming 輪班的每 'those who take turns'. The line is a fragment, and I read it as 'the officer of the turn, [speaking] to his own turn-servers'; the verb comes in the next unit.

morph.gloss: own, self [自己 裏(自的)行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (the (i) before it is Shiratori's)

sentences.t: kešigten-i bügüdgežü kešig orožu
sentences.l: Guardsmen (acc.) making-complete, turn entering,
sentences.i: should muster the guardsmen in full and go on duty,
sentences.n: bügüdgežü, Ming 點全着 ('count them all'), is the glossary's bügüdge- 'to muster, count over' (stem uncertain; compare bügüde 'all') + the converb -žü; the sense 'make complete, muster' is from the Ming. orožu is oro- + the converb -žu.

morph.gloss: guardsman, member of the guard [護衞的每 行]
to muster, count over (stem uncertain; compare bügüde 'all') [點全着]

sentences.t: γurban qonoldužu jeġüdgeldütügei.
sentences.l: Three spending-the-night-together, let-exchange-with-one-another.
sentences.i: and after three nights together let them relieve one another.
sentences.n: qonoldužu is qono- 'pass the night' + -ldu- 'together' + the converb -žu (Ming 共宿着). jeġüdgeldütügei is jeġüdge- 'to change' (stem uncertain, Ming 換) + -ldü- 'one another' + the optative -tügei (Ming 者). 'Three' has no noun; the Ming reads 三 only, and I supply 'nights' from qono-. Shiratori's closing mark for this speech comes later, on ileje.

sentences.t: Kešigtü küġün kešig hoγ̇araγ̇asu tere kešig oγ̇araγsan kešigtü-ji γurban beriġes süitügei.
sentences.l: Guard-having man turn if-missing, that turn having-missed guard-having (acc.) three rods let-instruct.
sentences.i: If a man of the guard misses his turn, let that man who missed his turn be given three strokes of the rod.
sentences.n: kešigtü is kešig + the possessive -tü 'having', the Ming 護衞有的, 'one who has the guard' (a man of the guard). hoγ̇araγ̇asu is hoγ̇ara- + the conditional -γ̇asu 'if' (Ming 脫了呵, 'if he slips off'); the stem is inferred from the Ming 脫, 'slip off, miss'. oγ̇araγsan is the same verb printed without h, with the past participle -γsan, 'the one who missed'. kešigtü-ji takes the accusative -ji after -ü (Ming 行). beriġes is 'rods' (Ming 條子). süitügei is the optative of süi- (Ming 敎導, 'instruct'); the stem is uncertain, and 'be given strokes of the rod' is my reading of the Ming 條子 with 敎導; the Ming does not say 'strike'.

morph.gloss: turn of duty, guard [護衞 有的]
to miss, fall short (stem inferred from the Ming 脫了 "slip off") [脫了呵]
to miss, fall short (printed without h) [脫了的]
turn of duty, guard [護衞的 行]
to give (rods)? (stem uncertain; Ming 敎導 "instruct") [敎導者︀]

sentences.t: Mün kešigtü basa nögöġete kešig hoγ̇araγ̇asu doloγ̇an beriġes süitügei.
sentences.l: Just guard-having again second-time turn if-missing, seven rods let-instruct.
sentences.i: If the same man misses a second turn again, let him be given seven strokes of the rod.
sentences.n: Mün kešigtü is 'that same man of the guard' (Ming 只, 'the very'). nögöġete is nögöġe 'second' + -te, taken as 'the second time' (Ming 第次). doloγ̇an is 'seven'. The rest is as in the previous unit.

morph.gloss: turn of duty, guard [扈衞 有的]
to miss, fall short (stem inferred from the Ming 脫了 "slip off") [脫了呵]
to give (rods)? (stem uncertain; Ming 敎導 "instruct") [敎導者︀]

sentences.t: Basa mün küġün beje γad ebečin ügei kešig-ün nojad-tur eje ügeġü
sentences.l: Again that-very man body-body illness without, of-turn officers-to counsel without,
sentences.i: Again, the same man, with no sickness of body and without having taken counsel with the officers of the turn,
sentences.n: A clause with no verb of its own: it qualifies the next unit, where the conditional hoγ̇araγ̇asu stands, so `i` has no 'if' here. beje γad ebečin ügei: beje 'body' and γad (Ming 體) make a pair, 'body', and ebečin ügei is 'without illness' (ügei, 'there is not'); the Ming reads 身體病無. nojad-tur is nojan with plural -d and dative-locative -tur, 'to the officers' (Ming 官人每行). eje ügeġü, Ming 商量無, 'counsel not'. I read it as 'having had no consultation'.

morph.gloss: body (Ming 體; paired with beje) [體]

sentences.t: basa mün kešigtü γurbanta kešig hoγ̇araγ̇asu γučin doloγ̇an beriġes šöjüġed
sentences.l: Again just guard-having three-times turn if-missing, thirty seven rods having-instructed,
sentences.i: if the same guardsman misses his turn again, a third time, having been given thirty-seven strokes of the rod,
sentences.n: γurbanta is γurban 'three' + -ta; the Ming 三次 and 'three times' are the evidence, the ending is uncertain. γučin doloγ̇an is 'thirty-seven'. šöjüġed (Ming 敎導了) is the converb of completed action -ġed on a verb that I take to be the one in süitügei; the stem (šöjü- / süi-) is uncertain, so 'having given' is only my reading of the Ming. This is the first half of a sentence that finishes in the next two units.

morph.gloss: turn of duty, guard [扈衞 有的]
to miss, fall short (stem inferred from the Ming 脫了 "slip off") [脫了呵]
to give (rods)? (stem uncertain; Ming 敎導, perhaps the verb of süitügei) [敎導了]

sentences.t: bidan-dur jabuqui-ban berkešijen ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: To-us own-going finding-hard was.
sentences.i: and was finding it hard to go about in our presence,
sentences.n: bidan-dur is bida 'we' (inclusive; the stem takes -n- before case) + the dative-locative -dur, 'to us', here 'in our presence'. jabuqui-ban is jabu- 'go' + the participle + the reflexive-possessive -ban 'one's own'. berkešijen is read as berkešije- 'to find hard' (the verb of berkešijeġsü in §§224–226; Ming 作難) + the converb -n; ažuγ̇u (Ming 有來) is the past 'was'. The -jen might be taken for the reflexive-possessive, but the verb berkešije- is already in the glossary, so I read it as stem + -n. 'Was finding it hard to go about in our presence' is uncertain, and the conditional force is carried by the unit before.

morph.gloss: to go, move about [行的 自的行]
to find hard, make difficulty (from berke 'hard') [作難︀]

sentences.t: Ečine qolo γažar-a ileje" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Behind far land-to let-us-send" saying decree became.
sentences.i: let us send him to a far-off land in the rear,” he said, and so decreed.
sentences.n: ečine 'behind, at the back' (Ming 背處) and qolo 'far' qualify γažar-a, 'to the land' (dative-locative -a). ileje is ile- 'send' with the hortative -je, 'let us send' (Ming 敎去咱). The closing quotation mark on ileje closes the speech opened at Kešig (before ororun). keġen žarliγ bolba, 'saying a decree became', is the stock close of a decree and I render it 'he said, and so decreed'.

sentences.t: "Kešiġüd-ün ötöküs γutaγ̇ar γutaγ̇ar kešig-tür ene žarliγ kešigten-e sonosγadqun.
sentences.l: "Of-turns heads third third in-turn this decree to-guardsmen make-hear (you).
sentences.i: “Heads of the turns, in every third turn, make this decree heard by the guardsmen.
sentences.n: The opening quotation mark on Kešiġüd-ün is Shiratori's. γutaγ̇ar γutaγ̇ar is 'third third' (Ming 第三 第三); 'every third turn' is my reading of the repetition. kešig-tür is the dative-locative 'in the turn'. sonosγadqun is sonos- 'to hear' + the causative -γa- 'make hear' (the Ming 敎聽) + -dqun, the polite plural command, 'you (all) …'.

morph.gloss: turn of duty, watch (Ming 護衞 "guards") [班每 的]
guardsman, member of the guard [宿衞的每 行]

sentences.t: Ese sonosγaγ̇asu kešiġüd-ün ötöküs aldaltan boltuγai.
sentences.l: Not if-made-to-hear, of-turns heads penalty-having let-be.
sentences.i: If they have not made it heard, let the heads of the turns be liable to a penalty.
sentences.n: ese is the negative of a past act ('not yet'); sonosγaγ̇asu is the causative again + the conditional -γ̇asu 'if'. aldaltan is aldal 'fault, penalty' + the possessive plural -tan (Ming 罰有的每, 'those with a penalty'), and boltuγai the optative 'let it be'. 'Liable to a penalty' follows aldal 'penalty' + -tan 'those having'.

morph.gloss: turn of duty, watch (Ming 護衞 "guards") [班每 的]

sentences.t: Žarliγ sonosuγ̇ad bürün dabaγ̇asu žariγ-un josu-γ̇ar kešig hoγ̇araγ̇asu kešigten aldaltan boltuγai" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Decree having-heard being, if-transgress, of-decree by-rule, turn if-missing, guardsmen penalty-having let-be" saying decree became.
sentences.i: If, having heard the decree, they transgress it, or if they miss their turn, let the guardsmen be liable to a penalty by the rule of the decree,” he said, and so decreed.
sentences.n: A long sentence, cut here at the stock close. sonosuγ̇ad bürün is 'having heard, being' (the converb of completed action -uγ̇ad and bü- 'be' + -rün), the Ming 聽了有. dabaγ̇asu is daba- 'cross over, transgress' (Ming 越了) + the conditional. Shiratori prints žariγ-un, without the l of žarliγ; the Ming and the sense agree. josu-γ̇ar is josu 'custom, rule' with the instrumental -γ̇ar (Ming 道理依着). The closing mark on boltuγai closes the speech opened at Kešiġüd-ün. Whether 'by the rule of the decree' belongs to the clause before it or to the one after it is not clear from the form.

morph.gloss: converb of completed action: having heard
to cross over, transgress (Ming 越) [越了呵]
command, decree (printed žariγ, without the l) [聖旨的]
custom, rule, proper way [道理 依着]
to miss, fall short (stem inferred from the Ming 脫了 "slip off") [脫了呵]
guardsman, member of the guard [護衞的每]

sentences.t: Kešiġüd-ün ötöküs aqalaγdaba ele keġen
sentences.l: Of-turns heads (they) were-made-heads indeed, saying,
sentences.i: “Heads of the turns, saying ‘We have become the seniors, after all,’
sentences.n: A second speech, with its opening mark omitted in the print; I supply it in `i` (the closing mark comes at qariγ̇ultuγai). aqalaγdaba is aqa 'elder' + the verb-maker -la- (as in aqalažu in §§224–226) + -γda- (a passive, tentative) + the past -ba (Ming 爲長了, 'has become the head'). ele (Ming 但) is an emphatic particle, 'only, indeed'. keġen closes the quotation. I read it as the Qahan quoting the heads' boast, 'we are the seniors', in order to forbid what follows.

morph.gloss: turn of duty, watch (Ming 護衞 "guards") [班每 的]
elder brother, elder (the noun the verb is made from) [爲長了]

sentences.t: sačaγ̇un oroγsad min-u kešigten-i na-dāča eje ügei bu hoṅžidudqun.
sentences.l: Equals those-who-entered, my guardsmen (acc.), from-me counsel without, do-not you-reproach.
sentences.i: do not reproach my guardsmen, who have entered as equals, without counsel from me.
sentences.n: sačaγ̇un (Ming 同等每) is 'alike, equal'. oroγsad is oro- 'enter' + the plural past participle -γsad, 'those who entered'. min-u is the genitive of bi, 'my' (stem min- + -u); here it stands before kešigten-i (Ming 我的). na-dāča is 'from me', with the ablative -dāča (Ming 我行; the glossary also has 比我, 'than me', for this word). bu is the prohibitive. hoṅžidudqun is a verb of reproach (stem uncertain; Ming 怪責) + the polite plural command -dqun.

morph.gloss: past participle, plural: those who have …
guardsman, member of the guard [扈衞的每 行]
to reproach, blame (stem uncertain; Ming 怪責) [怪責者︀您]

sentences.t: Žasa kündeġesü na-da žiγ̇adqun.
sentences.l: Rule if-stirred, to-me you-tell.
sentences.i: If the law is disturbed, tell me.
sentences.n: žasa is 'law, rule' (Ming 法度). kündeġesü is kündeġe- 'be moved, stirred' (Ming 動) + the conditional; 'disturbed' keeps the literal 'stirred'; that the law is breached is only my reading. na-da is 'to me' (bi with stem na- + the dative-locative -da). žiγ̇adqun is 'tell' (Ming 吿) + -dqun.

morph.gloss: law, rule, regulation (the Ming 法度) [法度]
to be moved, stirred (Ming 動) [動着呵]

sentences.t: Mököriġülkün josutan böġesü bida mököriġülü-že.
sentences.l: Cut-down-ones right-having if-be, we have-cut-down-indeed.
sentences.i: If there are those who deserve execution, and rightly so, we shall have them executed.
sentences.n: mököriġülkün (Ming 合處斬的, 'those who deserve execution') is read as mököri- 'cut down' + the causative -ġül- + a participle; the stem is inferred from the Ming. josutan is josu 'right, reason' + the possessive plural -tan (Ming 理有的每, 'those with reason'), read 'rightly so'; the other reading, 'those who are in the right', would turn the sentence upside down and does not suit the Ming 合處斬的, böġesü is bü- 'be' + the conditional, bida 'we' (inclusive). mököriġülü-že is the same verb ending in -ü and the particle -že 'indeed'. The sense, uncertain in its detail, is that execution is for those who deserve it with reason.

morph.gloss: to cut down (stem inferred from the Ming 處斬 "execute") [合處斬的]

sentences.t: Nišiγdaqun josutan böġesü kebteġülžü nišid-že.
sentences.l: Strike-ones right-having if-be, making-lie-down strike-indeed.
sentences.i: If there are those who deserve a beating, and rightly so, we shall lay them down and beat them.
sentences.n: nišiγdaqun (Ming 合打的每, 'those who deserve a beating') and nišid-že (Ming 打也者) both come from a stem niši- 'strike', which is inferred from the Ming 打; the endings (-γda- as a passive, -d as perhaps 'we') are tentative. kebteġülžü is kebte- 'lie down' + the causative -ġül- + the converb -žü (Ming 敎臥着, 'making them lie down'). josutan böġesü is as in the last unit, 'if there are (those) with reason', that is, rightly so.

morph.gloss: to strike (stem inferred from the Ming 打) [合打的每]

sentences.t: Aqalaba ele keġežü sačaγ̇un kešigten-i
sentences.l: Were-heads indeed saying, equals guardsmen (acc.),
sentences.i: Saying ‘I have become the senior, after all,’ if anyone, in the case of my guardsmen who are his equals,
sentences.n: aqalaba is aqa + -la- + the past -ba, Ming 爲長了, with no person ending (so 'I' is my reading); ele is 'indeed'. keġežü is keġe- + converb 'saying'. sačaγ̇un kešigten-i is 'equals, guardsmen (accusative)'. The sentence runs through the next two units: whoever, saying so, strikes my guardsmen with hand, foot or rod. I have broken the chain here.

morph.gloss: elder brother, elder (the noun the verb is made from) [爲長了]
guardsman, member of the guard [護衞的(每)行]

sentences.t: min-u öġer-ün γar köl kürgežü beriġedešü
sentences.l: My own hand foot delivering, if-rod-strike,
sentences.i: he brings his own hand and foot to bear on them, or strikes them with a rod,
sentences.n: öġer-ün is öġer 'own' with the genitive -ün after r; γar köl is 'hand, foot' (Ming 手 腳). kürgežü (Ming 敎到着) is kürge- 'deliver' (uncertain) + the converb: 'delivering [a blow]'. beriġedešü (Ming 條子打呵, 'if one strikes with a rod') is from beriġe 'rod' with a verb-maker and the conditional; the stem is read from the Ming. min-u closes the phrase kešigten-i min-u, 'my guardsmen', begun in the last unit: the genitive stands after its noun, as the glossary has it.

sentences.t: beriġe-jin qariγ̇u beriġe kü nudurγa-jin qariγ̇u mudrγa kü qariγ̇ultuγai" keġebe.
sentences.l: Rod's return rod indeed, fist's return fist indeed, let-be-repaid," said.
sentences.i: let the answer to a rod be a rod, and the answer to a fist a fist,” he said.
sentences.n: beriġe-jin is the genitive 'of the rod' (-jin after a vowel; Ming 的) and nudurγa-jin the same for 'fist'; Shiratori prints mudrγa for the last 'fist', a slip for nudurγa (the Han transcription is the same). qariγ̇u is 'answer, return' (Ming 囘). kü is the emphatic particle (Ming 也). qariγ̇ultuγai is a qariγ̇u- verb in the optative (Ming 敎囘者, 'let it be returned'); the stem is uncertain. The closing mark on qariγ̇ultuγai ends the speech whose opening mark I supplied at Kešiġüd-ün, and keġebe 'said' reports it.

morph.gloss: fist (printed mudrγa, a slip for nudurγa) [拳頭]

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan decree becoming-when:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan issued a decree:
sentences.n: bolurun is bol- 'to become' with the converb of time -urun, 'when'. The same decree opener as at the start of §229 (§227 begins with bolžu); the Ming has 做 only.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Γadanadus miṅγad-un nojad-ača min-u kešigtü deġere bi-že.
sentences.l: "Outside-ones of-thousands officers-than my guard-having above is-indeed.
sentences.i: “My guardsman is above the officers of the thousands who are outside.
sentences.n: Shiratori's opening mark is on Γadanadus (Ming 在外每, 'those outside'); I carry it in `i`. γadanadus is γadana 'outside' + a plural ending (-dus, uncertain). miṅγad-un nojad-ača is 'than the officers of the thousands', with the ablative -ača (Ming 行), 'compared with'. kešigtü is 'the man of the guard'. deġere is 'above' and bi-že 'is indeed' (bü- 'to be' in the form bi- before -že). The comparison is with the thousand-commanders posted outside.

sentences.t: Γadanadus žaγ̇ud-un, harbad-un nojad-ača min-u kešigtü-jin kötöčin deġere bi-že.
sentences.l: Outside-ones of-hundreds of-tens officers-than my guard-having's companion above is-indeed.
sentences.i: The companion of my guardsman is above the officers of the hundreds and of the tens who are outside.
sentences.n: The same pattern at the next two ranks: žaγ̇ud-un, 'of the hundreds' and harbad-un, 'of the tens'. kešigtü-jin kötöčin is 'the guard's companion' (Ming 護衞有的的 伴當): kešigtü + the genitive -jin, then kötöčin, 'companion, attendant'. So even a guardsman's attendant outranks the lower officers outside.

morph.gloss: turn of duty, guard [護衞有的的]

sentences.t: Min-u kešigten-dür γadanadus miṅγaliγ̇ud sačaγ̇un bolžu deṅgečen
sentences.l: My guardsmen-to outside thousand-having-ones equals being, level,
sentences.i: The thousand-commanders outside, being equals of my guardsmen, on a level with them,
sentences.n: A condition set out before the verb. kešigten-dür is the dative-locative 'to / with my guardsmen' (Ming 護衞的行). miṅγaliγ̇ud (Ming 千戶每) is miṅγan 'thousand' + endings, 'thousand-commanders'; the analysis is tentative. sačaγ̇un bolžu deṅgečen is 'equal, being, level' (Ming 同等每 做着 比肩).

morph.gloss: guardsman, member of the guard [護衞的(每)行]

sentences.t: min-u kešigtü-dür kereldüġesü miṅγaloγ̇udai küġün-i ereġüleje" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: My guard-having-to if-fighting, of-thousand-commanders man (acc.) let-us-blame" saying decree became.
sentences.i: if they fight with my guardsman, let us hold the thousand-commanders' man guilty,” he said, and so decreed.
sentences.n: kereldüġesü is kerel- 'quarrel' (Ming 鬪毆, 'fight') + -ldü- 'with one another' + the conditional -ġesü. miṅγaloγ̇udai is taken as miṅγan 'thousand' + endings + -ai, a genitive (tentative; Ming 千戶每的), 'of the thousand-commanders', qualifying küġün-i, 'the man (object)'. ereġüleje is a verb 'to blame, hold guilty' (inferred from Ming 罪) + the hortative -je, 'let us …'. The closing mark on ereġüleje closes the speech opened at Γadanadus.

morph.gloss: to quarrel, fight (Ming 鬪毆) [鬪毆呵]
to blame, hold guilty (stem inferred from the Ming 罪) [罪咱]

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan decree becoming-when:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan issued a decree:
sentences.n: The decree opener once more.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Kešig kešiġüd-ün nojad-ta žarliγ tuṅγarun
sentences.l: "Turn of-turns officers-to decree proclaiming-when,
sentences.i: “When proclaiming the decree to the officers of the turns,
sentences.n: Shiratori's opening mark is on Kešig. The Ming has 班 for each of the two kešig words (班 班每的 官人每行); I read kešig kešiġüd-ün as 'the turn, of the turns', a doubled phrase. nojad-ta is nojan with plural -d and dative-locative -ta (Ming 官人每行). tuṅγarun is 'when proclaiming'.

morph.gloss: turn of duty, watch (Ming 護衞 "guards") [班每 的]

sentences.t: qorčin turγaγ̇ud kešig orožu
sentences.l: Quiver-bearers day-guards turn entering,
sentences.i: the quiver-bearers and the day guards, having gone on duty,
sentences.n: qorčin (Ming 帶弓箭的, 'those with bow and arrows') is read qor 'quiver' + -či + the plural, 'quiver-bearers'; turγaγ̇ud is the plural of turγaγ 'day guard'. orožu is the converb 'entering'.

sentences.t: üdür-ün jabudal žüg žüg mör mör-tür(i)-jen jabužu
sentences.l: Of-day going each each track, to-own-post going,
sentences.i: going about by day, in each direction, each to his own post,
sentences.n: üdür-ün is üdür 'day' with the genitive; jabudal (Ming 行) is a verbal noun of jabu- 'go' and the reading is tentative. žüg žüg is 'each each' (Ming 各 各); mör is 'track' (Ming 道子) and mör-tür(i)-jen 'to one's own track', read as 'post' (Ming 道子 自的行), with the dative-locative and the reflexive -jen. jabužu is the converb 'going'.

morph.gloss: going, movement, doing (jabu- "go" + -dal, verbal noun; tentative) [行]
track, post of duty [道子 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (the (i) before it is Shiratori's)

sentences.t: naran-u γaltaj-a kebteġül-e žailažü γadana γaržu qonotuγai.
sentences.l: Of-sun in-the-light night-guard-to giving-way, outside going-out, let-them-pass-night.
sentences.i: and while the sun gives light, giving way to the night guard, go outside and spend the night there.
sentences.n: naran-u is naran 'sun' + the genitive; γaltaj-a (Ming 光有(的)行) is read as γal 'fire, light' + the possessive -tai + the dative-locative -a, 'in the light', but the literal sense is 'while the sun has light'; that this means dusk is only a guess. kebteġül-e is 'to the night guard' (dative-locative -e, front-vowel form). žailažü is a verb of giving way (Ming 躱, 'avoid, step aside') + the converb; γaržu is γar- 'go out' + converb; qonotuγai is qono- 'pass the night' + the optative.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (the -u form after a stem in n)
to give way, step aside (Ming 躱 "avoid") [躱着]

sentences.t: Bidan-dur süni kebteġül qonan atuγai.
sentences.l: To-us at-night night-guard spending-the-night let-be.
sentences.i: Let the night guard stay with us through the night.
sentences.n: bidan-dur is 'to us' (bida with -n- and the dative-locative); süni 'night' (Ming 夜) is placed before kebteġül, 'night guard' (Ming 宿衞, from kebte- 'to lie down'). qonan is qono- + the converb -n, 'spending the night'; atuγai is a- 'be, stay' + the optative.

morph.gloss: night guard, those who lie down [宿衞]

sentences.t: Qorčin qor baγ̇určin ajaγa saba kebteġül-e taγ̇ulžu odtuγai.
sentences.l: Quiver-bearers quiver, cooks cup dish, to-night-guard handing-over, let-go.
sentences.i: The quiver-bearers their quivers, the cooks their cups and dishes: handing them over to the night guard, let them go.
sentences.n: qor 'quiver' (Ming 箭筒), ajaγa 'cup' (Ming 器) and saba 'dish' (Ming 皿). baγ̇určin is 'cook' (Ming 厨子). taγ̇ulžu is taγ̇ul- 'hand over' (Ming 分付) + converb, and odtuγai is od- 'go' + the optative. The objects are bare nouns, with no accusative.

morph.gloss: to hand over (Ming 分付) [分付着]

sentences.t: Γadana qonoγsad qorčin turγaγ̇ud baγ̇určin bidan-i sülen idetele kirüġe-dür
sentences.l: Outside those-who-passed-the-night quiver-bearers day-guards cooks, us (acc.) soup until-eating, to-gathering-place,
sentences.i: Those who have spent the night outside, the quiver-bearers, day guards and cooks, until they have eaten soup with us, at the gathering place,
sentences.n: Opens with Γadana (Ming 外行), 'outside'. qonoγsad is qono- + the plural past participle, 'those who spent the night'. bidan-i is 'us' with the accusative -i (Ming 俺行). sülen 'soup' (Ming 湯). idetele is ide- 'eat' + -tele 'until' (Ming 喫 直到). kirüġe-dür (Ming 聚馬, 'assembled horses') is read as a place of gathering, 'at the gathering place'; the sense is uncertain. 'With us' for bidan-i is my reading of the sense: the accusative 'us' is the form, and its role with idetele is not clear. The sentence continues through the next two units.

morph.gloss: to pass the night [宿了的每]
past participle, plural: those who have …
gathering (Ming 聚馬 "assembled horses"; sense uncertain) [聚馬]

sentences.t: saγ̇užu kebteġül-dür kelečilešü
sentences.l: Sitting, to-night-guard conversing,
sentences.i: sitting and conversing with the night guard,
sentences.n: saγ̇užu is saγ̇u- 'sit' + converb. kebteġül-dür is 'to the night guard'. kelečilešü (Ming 通話着) is a verb of speaking in the converb; the stem is tentative, and the ending -šü (not -žü) is as Shiratori prints it.

morph.gloss: to speak, converse (stem tentative; Ming 通話) [通話着]

sentences.t: sülen iden baraγ̇asu
sentences.l: Soup eating when-finished,
sentences.i: and when they have finished eating the soup,
sentences.n: iden is ide- 'eat' with the converb -n; baraγ̇asu is bara- 'be finished' used as an auxiliary + the conditional -γ̇asu, 'when done' (Ming 了呵).

sentences.t: qorčin qor-tur turγaγ saγ̇urin-dur(i)-jan baγ̇určin ajaγa saba-dur(i)-jan taγ̇araldutuγai.
sentences.l: Quiver-bearers to-quiver day-guard to-own-seat, cooks cup dish to-own let-return-together.
sentences.i: Let the quiver-bearers go back to their quivers, the day guards to their own seats, the cooks to their own cups and dishes, each to his own.
sentences.n: The datives decide the sense: qor-tur is 'to the quiver', saγ̇urin-dur(i)-jan 'to one's own seat', saba-dur(i)-jan 'to one's own dish', so the men go back to their things (Ming 復, 'return, resume'). The Ming glosses are 箭筒行 散班 坐位自的行 and 厨子 器 皿自的行. taγ̇araldutuγai is a verb of returning (stem uncertain) + -ldu- ('jointly', perhaps 'each') + the optative. The reflexives are -jan, with the vowel (i) set before it by Shiratori. What is meant by the quivers and dishes being 'returned to' is not certain.

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive: one's own (the (i) before it is Shiratori's)
reflexive-possessive: one's own (the (i) before it is Shiratori's)
to return, restore (stem tentative; Ming 復) [復者︀]

sentences.t: Kešig kešig oroqun mün mün josu-γ̇ar ene qaγ̇uli-bar tein kitügei" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Turn turn those-who-enter just just by-rule this by-custom so let-do" saying decree became.
sentences.i: Let those who go on duty, turn after turn, do the same, by the rule and by this custom,” he said, and so decreed.
sentences.n: Kešig kešig (Ming 班 班) is 'turn, turn'. oroqun is oro- + the participle -qun, 'the ones who enter'. mün mün (Ming 只 只) is 'just, just'. josu-γ̇ar is 'by the rule' and qaγ̇uli-bar 'by the custom' (Ming 軆例 依着), both instrumentals (-γ̇ar on josu, -bar on qaγ̇uli; I do not explain the difference of form). tein is 'so, thus'. kitügei is ki- 'do' + the optative -tügei (Ming 做者), 'let them do'. The speech opened at Kešig (before nojad-ta); Shiratori's closing mark is on kitügei.

morph.gloss: custom, rule, proper way [理 依着]
rule, custom, practice (Ming 軆例) [軆例 依着]

sentences.t: "Naran šiṅgegsen-ü qoina ordo-jin qoinaγ̇un uridaγ̇un ketügelčen jabuqu küġün-i barižu
sentences.l: "Sun of-having-set after of-palace behind in-front crosswise going man (acc.) seizing,
sentences.i: “After the sun has set, a man going about the palace from behind, from in front, or crosswise, seizing him,
sentences.n: Opens with Shiratori's mark on Naran. šiṅgegsen-ü is a past participle (šiṅge- 'set', stem tentative, Ming 落) + the genitive, 'of the set': 'after the sun has set'. qoina 'after, behind' and ordo-jin 'of the palace' (Ming 宮的). qoinaγ̇un and uridaγ̇un (Ming 從後, 從前) are 'from behind' and 'from in front' (qoina and urida + -γ̇un in the glossary), with an ending I cannot explain. ketügelčen (Ming 橫越) 'crossing'. jabuqu küġün-i is 'the man who walks' + accusative. barižu is bari- 'seize' + converb. barižu occurs twice: here it ends the clause about the man, and the next unit repeats it with kebteġül.

morph.gloss: to set, sink (of the sun; stem tentative, Ming 落) [落了的]
crosswise, across (Ming 橫越; the shape is uncertain) [橫越]
to take hold of, seize [拿着]

sentences.t: kebteġül barižu qonožu manaγar-i kebteġül üges in-ü asaγtuγai.
sentences.l: Night-guard seizing, spending-the-night, next-morning night-guard his words let-ask.
sentences.i: let the night guard, having seized him and passed the night, ask him in the morning for his words.
sentences.n: kebteġül barižu is 'the night guard, seizing', or 'holding [him] for the night guard'; the Ming 宿衞 拿着 does not say which. qonožu is qono- + converb. manaγar-i is 'the next morning' (Ming 明早行). üges in-ü is 'words, his': üges has the plural -s, and in-ü is the third-person genitive, placed after its noun (the front-vowel companion of the back-vowel an-u). asaγtuγai is asaγ- 'ask' + the optative.

morph.gloss: night guard, those who lie down [宿衞]
to take hold of, seize [拿着]
night guard, those who lie down [宿衞]
his, her, their (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.t: Kebteġül kešig jeġüdgeldürün belge an-u daγ̇ulžu orožu iretügei.
sentences.l: Night-guard turn when-changing sign their handing-over, entering let-come.
sentences.i: When the night-guard shift is relieved, let them come in, handing over their token.
sentences.n: jeġüdgeldürün is jeġüdge- 'change' + -ldü- + -rün, 'when relieving one another'. belge is 'sign, token' (Ming 符驗) and an-u 'their'. daγ̇ulžu (Ming 分付着) is 'handing over'; orožu 'entering'; iretügei is ire- 'come' + the optative -tügei. Kešig is placed next to kebteġül as in the Ming (宿衞 班), so I read kebteġül kešig as 'the night-guard shift' (the glossary also has kešig as 'the guard').

morph.gloss: night guard, those who lie down [宿衞]
his, their (back-vowel third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to hand over (Ming 分付; printed daγ̇ul-, the same word as taγ̇ul-) [分付着]

sentences.t: Jeġüdgežü γarqun kebteġül taγ̇ulžu kü γarču odtuγai" keġebe.
sentences.l: Having-changed, those-going-out night-guard handing-over indeed going-out let-go" said.
sentences.i: Those who go out after changing over are to hand over to the night guard, and go out,” he said.
sentences.n: jeġüdgežü is the converb 'changing'. γarqun is γar- 'go out' + the participle -qun, 'those going out'. taγ̇ulžu 'handing over'. kü (Ming 也) is the emphatic particle, 'indeed'; I leave it unrendered in `i`. γarču is the converb of γar- written -ču. odtuγai is the optative 'let (them) go'. The closing mark on odtuγai ends the quotation opened at Naran, and keġebe 'said' reports it.

morph.gloss: night guard, those who lie down [宿衞]
to hand over (Ming 分付) [分付着]

sentences.t: "Kebteġül süni ordo horčin kebtežü egüden daružu baiγsad
sentences.l: "Night-guard at-night palace round lying, door pressing, the-standing-ones,
sentences.i: “The night guards, lying round the palace at night, pressing on the door, those who have taken their stand,
sentences.n: A new speech opens on Kebteġül (Shiratori's mark). horčin is 'around' (Ming 周圍) and ordo 'palace'. kebtežü is kebte- 'lie down' + converb. egüden 'door'. daružu is daru- 'press down, hold' (Ming 壓着) + converb. baiγsad is bai- 'stand' + the plural past participle -γsad (Ming 立了的每), 'those who have stood'.

morph.gloss: night guard, those who lie down [宿衞]
to press down, hold (Ming 壓) [壓着]
past participle, plural: those who have …

sentences.t: kebteġül süni oroqun haran-i ekid an-u dalbaru mürüs an-u baγ̇utala čabčižu oγ̇orudqun.
sentences.l: Night-guard at-night entering people (acc.) heads their smashing, shoulder-blades their until-falling, hewing, go-off (you all).
sentences.i: the night guard are to drive off the people who enter at night, smashing their heads and hewing at their shoulders until they fall.
sentences.n: The hardest unit of the part. oroqun is oro- + the participle, 'the one entering'; haran-i is 'the people (object)'. ekid (Ming 腦每, 'brains') I read as 'heads'; dalbaru (Ming 打破) 'breaking, smashing'; mürüs (Ming 肩甲) 'shoulder-blades', with the plural -s; baγ̇utala is baγ̇u- 'fall' + -tala 'until'. an-u 'their'. čabčižu is čabči- 'hew' + converb. oγ̇orudqun, Ming 去了您, is read as oγ̇oru- 'go off' (stem uncertain) with -dqun, the polite plural command, literally 'go off, you (all)'; 'drive off' is a guess from the Ming 去了 and the context, and I do not know what the object is. čabčižu has the Ming 欲着 ('wishing'), not the 斬 of the glossary's čabči-; a slip is probable, and the reading 'hew' is uncertain. The sentence is as the Ming gives it, and the drastic sense is plain.

morph.gloss: night guard, those who lie down [宿衞]
his, their (back-vowel third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
smashing, breaking (Ming 打破; form uncertain) [打破]
his, their (back-vowel third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to come down, fall [落下直到]
to hew, cut down (stem inferred; the Ming 欲 is perhaps a slip for 斬) [欲着]
to go off, be gone (stem inferred from the Ming 去了) [去了您]

sentences.t: Jaγ̇aral keleten haran süni ireġesü kebteġül-dür keleležü
sentences.l: Urgent word-having people at-night if-come, to-night-guard speaking,
sentences.i: If people with urgent words come at night, speaking to the night guard,
sentences.n: jaγ̇aral (Ming 急忙) is 'in haste, urgent'. keleten is kele 'tongue, word' + the possessive plural -ten, 'those having words' (Ming 言語有的). haran is 'people, persons'; ireġesü is ire- 'come' + the conditional -ġesü, 'if (he) comes'. keleležü is kele- + a verb-maker + converb, 'speaking'. 'People with words' are messengers (my reading).

morph.gloss: urgent, in haste (Ming 急忙) [急忙]

sentences.t: ger-ün ümerēče kebteġül-lüġe qamtu baižu keleleġültügei" keġebe.
sentences.l: Of-house from-behind with-night-guard together standing, let-be-made-to-speak" said.
sentences.i: standing behind the tent together with the night guard, let them have it told,” he said.
sentences.n: ger-ün is 'of the tent' (genitive -ün). ümerēče is ümer 'behind' + the ablative -ēče (long ē), 'from behind' (the Ming 邊行 says only 'at the side'). kebteġül-lüġe is 'with the night guard' (comitative -lüġe, Ming 一同). qamtu 'together'. baižu 'standing'. keleleġültügei is a causative of kele- 'speak' in the optative (Ming 敎說者, 'let it be told'). keġebe closes the speech.

sentences.t: "Kebteġül-eče deġere saγ̇uri ken ber bu saγ̇utuγai.
sentences.l: "Than-the-night-guard above seat who even do-not let-sit.
sentences.i: “No one at all may sit in a seat above the night guard.
sentences.n: Shiratori's opening mark is on Kebteġül-eče. The ablative -eče (Ming 行) is 'than'. ken ber is 'who even', that is 'anyone', with the negative bu 'do not' (Ming 休). saγ̇uri is 'seat' and saγ̇utuγai is saγ̇u- 'sit' + the optative. The series of prohibitions that follows is the night guard's standing orders.

sentences.t: Kebteġül-eče kelen ügei ken ber bu orotuγai.
sentences.l: Than-the-night-guard word without, who even do-not let-enter.
sentences.i: No one at all may enter without a word from the night guard.
sentences.n: kebteġül-eče kelen ügei is 'without word from the night guard'; the ablative again with ügei 'without'. orotuγai is oro- 'enter' + the optative.

sentences.t: Kebteġül-ün degeġün ken ber bu jabutuγai.
sentences.l: Of-night-guard above, who even do-not let-go.
sentences.i: No one at all may walk above the night guard.
sentences.n: kebteġül-ün degeġün: 'the night guard's upper side' (Ming 從上, 'from above'). degeġün is a noun or postposition and I read it spatially, as the upper side of the guard (Ming 從上 says only 'from above').

morph.gloss: above, upper side (Ming 從上) [從上]

sentences.t: Kebteġül-ün žaγaγ̇un bu jabutuγai.
sentences.l: Of-night-guard between, do-not let-go.
sentences.i: Do not walk between the night guards.
sentences.n: žaγaγ̇un (Ming 兩間, 'between two') is 'the space between'; the sense is that no one is to pass between the guards. jabutuγai is jabu- 'go' + the optative; the Ming here is 行者︀ ('let go'), without the 敎 that the glossary records for the same form elsewhere.

morph.gloss: between, space between (Ming 兩間) [兩間]

sentences.t: Kebteġül-ün toγ̇a bu asaγtuγai.
sentences.l: Of-night-guard number, do-not let-ask.
sentences.i: Do not ask how many the night guard are.
sentences.n: toγ̇a 'number' (Ming 數). asaγtuγai is asaγ- 'ask' + the optative.

sentences.t: Kebteġül-ün degeġün jabuqun haran-i kebteġül barituγai.
sentences.l: Of-night-guard above going people (acc.), night-guard let-seize.
sentences.i: Let the night guard seize the people who walk above them.
sentences.n: jabuqun is jabu- + the participle -qun, 'the one who goes' (Ming 行的). haran-i is 'the people' with the accusative. barituγai is bari- 'seize' + the optative.

morph.gloss: above, upper side (Ming 從上) [從上]
night guard, those who lie down [宿衞]
to take hold of, seize [拿者︀]

sentences.t: Žaγaγ̇un jabuqun haran-i kebteġül barituγai.
sentences.l: Between going people (acc.), night-guard let-seize.
sentences.i: And let them seize those who go between them.
sentences.n: The same pattern as the last unit. Shiratori's capital on Žaγaγ̇un marks the start of a sentence.

morph.gloss: between, space between (Ming 兩間) [兩間]
night guard, those who lie down [宿衞]
to take hold of, seize [拿者︀]

sentences.t: Toγ̇a asaγuγsan küġün-i kebteġül tere küġün-i
sentences.l: Number having-asked man (acc.), night-guard that man (acc.)
sentences.i: As for the man who has asked the number — the night guard, that man —
sentences.n: asaγuγsan is asaγ- 'ask' + the past participle -γsan, 'the one who asked'. küġün-i 'the man' (accusative). The sentence goes on in the next unit, and the verb arrives only in abtuγai, 'let (the night guard) take'.

morph.gloss: past participle: the one who has asked
night guard, those who lie down [宿衞]

sentences.t: tere kü üdür-ün unuγsan aγta emeġeltü qadartu-ji emüšügsen qubčasun selte kebteġül abtuγai" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: That indeed day's ridden gelding saddle-having, bridle-having (acc.), worn clothing along-with, night-guard let-take" saying decree became.
sentences.i: together with the gelding he rode that very day, saddled and bridled, and the clothes he has on, let the night guard take,” he said, and so decreed.
sentences.n: tere kü üdür-ün is 'that very day's' (kü the emphatic particle; üdür-ün the genitive of üdür 'day', Ming 日的). unuγsan is unu- 'ride' + the past participle, 'ridden'. aγta is 'gelding'. emeġeltü is emeġel 'saddle' + the possessive -tü, 'saddled'; qadartu-ji is qadar 'bridle' (Ming 轡頭) + -tu 'having' + the accusative -ji, 'with bridle, as object'. emüšügsen is 'worn' and qubčasun 'clothing'. selte (Ming 連) 'along with'. abtuγai is ab- 'take' + the optative; its objects are not certain: the man himself (küġün-i, twice in the last unit) and/or his gelding and clothes. I read selte, 'along with', as joining the gelding and clothes to the man, so that all are taken; the other reading, that only the horse and clothes are taken from him, is possible. The closing mark on abtuγai ends the speech opened at Kebteġül-eče.

morph.gloss: bridle (Ming 轡頭) [轡頭 有的行]
night guard, those who lie down [宿衞]

sentences.t: Elžigedei itegeltü böġetele žilda kebteġül-ün degeġün jabuqu bolun kebteġül-e ker bariγdalaγ̇a.
sentences.l: Elžigedei reliance-having while-being, late of-night-guard above going being, by-night-guard how was-seized.
sentences.i: Eljigedei, being one with something to rely on, was walking late above the night guard, and how was he seized by the night guard?
sentences.n: A story about a named man. Elžigedei (Ming 人名) is 'Eljigedei'. itegeltü is itegel 'reliance' (Ming 倚仗, 'rely on') + the possessive -tü, 'having reliance'; what he relied on is not named. böġetele is bü- 'be' + -tele 'while'. žilda (Ming 悅, 'pleased') I take as 'late, evening', as the glossary does elsewhere (there the Ming is 晩); 悅 is probably a slip for 晩, and 'late' is uncertain. kebteġül-ün degeġün jabuqu bolun is 'being one who walks above the night guard'. bariγdalaγ̇a is bari- 'seize' + -γda- passive + a past ending (tentative), 'was seized'. ker 'how' (Ming 怎), I read it as a question 'how was he seized?', but it could also mean 'was seized in the manner (of the rule)'; this is uncertain. Shiratori ends the unit with a full stop, not a question mark, so whether it is a question is uncertain.

morph.gloss: reliance, trust (Ming 倚仗) [倚仗 有的]
to be (böġe- before an ending) [有間]
late, evening (as elsewhere; the Ming 悅 "pleased" here looks like a slip for 晩 "evening"; uncertain) [悅]
above, upper side (Ming 從上) [從上]
